descriptionSet.display: The fortified settlement of Ḩārat as-Sawāfah forms, along with the neighbouring quarter of al-Barāshid to the south, the eastern edge of the Sināw oasis, in the Ash Sharqīyah North Governorate. Sawāfah developed along Falaj al Mushaq with an extended north-south orientation with the palm groves to the west of the falaj channel. Originally enclosed within a continuous defensive wall with gates on the north, south and west walls, more openings have emerged to allow shortcuts to the agricultural fields from the new settlement developments beyond. The settlement presents two highly dilapidated gates on the downhill side, at the northern and southern ends respectively. A relatively regular street plan, consisting in main thoroughfares that spread out approximately orthogonally from a central open space, suggest a relatively recent development, in the eighteenth or the early- nineteenth century. Clearly delineated clusters laid out in both a north-south and east-west direction accommodate grand houses on two and three storeys. These are organised around courtyards and arcaded porticoes (līwāns), where daily domestic activities such as grinding, coffee making and weaving, the storage of produce and agricultural implements, sheltering of animal, as well as social activities would take place. Made of mud brick and stone, the buildings of as-Sawāfah present remarkable architectural and decorative features. These include generous arcades of pointed arches on round masonry columns, masonry lattice balustrades separating the courtyard from the shaded porticoes and high-quality workmanship of mouldings in sarūj, a traditional hydraulic render made of calcined clay and lime.
